AGENDA

OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA 90274
Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.

1.
Waive Further Reading
Recommendation: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first reading or adoption on second reading.
2.
Adoption of Ordinance 16-716 Adding Chapter 18.73 to Title 18 of the PVEMC Amending Section 18.12.030 and Adding Sections 18.04.021, 18.08.012, 18.16.060 and 18.37.050 in Order to Impose an Express Ban on Marijuana Cultivation, Delivery, and Dispensaries Within the City
Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council adopt on second reading Ordinance 16-716 adding Chapter 18.73 to Title 18 of the PVEMC amending Section 18.12.030 and adding Sections 18.04.021 18.08.012, 18.16.060 and 18.37.050 in order to impose an express ban on marijuana cultivation, delivery, and dispensaries within the City.
Staff Report
3.
Adoption of Resolution R16-10 Authorizing the Appropriation of Public Safety COPS Funds to Complete the Purchase of a Security Video Camera System for the Police Department
Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution R16-10 approving the use of FY14-15 COPS funds, and approve the appropriation of $48,504.79 of COPS fund to complete payment of the agreement with VAS Security Systems, Inc.
Staff Report
4.
Contract Award for PW-635-16; Trash TMDL Compliance for a Portion of Machado Lake Watershed Project
Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council award a construction contract in the amount of $20,407 to United Storm Water, Inc. for the completion of the Trash TMDL Compliance for a Portion of Machado Lake Watershed Project (PW-635-16) along with authorization of the $2,000 contingency.
Staff Report
5.
Approval of License Agreement with the City of Rolling Hills Estates for Utility Underground Cabling that Runs Onto City Property
Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council approve the license agreement with the City of Rolling Hills Estates to construct and maintain an underground cable system and authorize the City Manager to execute the license agreement.

9.

a.
WT-130-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment within the City right-of-way on the corner of Via Fernandez and Via Visalia.
Applicant: Crown Castle NG West LLC
300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
Irvine, CA 92618
Action: Approved the application (5-0 in favor) with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) The steel pole shall be burnished prior to painting. The pole and antennas must be painted a flat dark brown, and maintained in the same condition thereafter; 2) The CISH equipment cabinet should be painted dark green to blend in with the existing surrounding environment and nearby meter cabinets in the public right-of-way; 3) Crown Castle shall place its name on the lid of the proposed equipment vault; 4) All cables interconnecting the antennas and all transmission equipment should run within the replacement pole except as minimally required to connect to the antennas; 5) The replacement steel pole is not a wireless tower for any purpose, but rather it is considered only a replacement City street sign pole; 6) The steel pole shall be designated as a replacement for the existing pole to be removed, and after installation, the replacement pole shall be dedicated to the City for a fee of $1.00 so that it is clear for federal law purposes that replacement pole maintain its primary use and function as a City traffic sign support; 7) Permittee shall install and at all times maintain in good condition an â€œRF Noticeâ€ and â€œNetwork Operations Center Informationâ€ sign on the steel pole at approximately 14 feet AGL; 8) Permittee shall ensure that all RF signage complies with FCC OET Bulletin 65 or ANSI C95.2 for color, symbol, and content conventions; 9) Attached street signs shall be installed in accordance with the MUTCD (Manual Uniform Traffic Control Devices) California Edition; and 10) Attached street signs shall be with approved hardware per the Cityâ€™s Maintenance Foreman.
b.
WT-145-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment within the City right-of-way across from 801 Via Coronel.
Applicant: Crown Castle NG West LLC
300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
Irvine, CA 92618
Action: Approved the application (5-0 in favor) with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) The DAS nodes shall not be located on the pole and shall be located within a ground mounted CISH-51 cabinet; 2) The antenna must be painted a flat dark brown, and maintained in the same condition thereafter to match the existing wood pole; 3) All cables interconnecting the antennas and all transmission equipment should run vertically flush to the existing wood pole, except as minimally required to connect to the antennas; 4) The equipment cabinet should be painted a color to blend in with the existing surrounding environment and nearby meter cabinet in the public right-of-way; 5) Permittee shall install and at all times maintain in good condition an â€œRF Noticeâ€ and â€œNetwork Operations Center Informationâ€ sign on the wood pole at approximately 3 feet below the antenna; and 6) Permittee shall ensure that all RF signage complies with FCC OET Bulletin 65 or ANSI C95.2 for color, symbol, and content conventions.
c.
NC-1541/G-1559/M-1053/M-1066-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 2812 Victoria Place. Lot 16, Block 2450, Tract 7332. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.
Applicant: Rosa Velazquez
118 S. Catalina Ave., #N
Redondo Beach, CA 90277
Owner: Ebrahim Soltani
Action: Approved, in part, the application (5-0 in favor) with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) A license agreement shall be submitted to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the city, its officers, agents and employees from and against any and all loss, damage, liability, claims, demands, costs, charges, and expenses, including attorneyâ€™s fees, and causes of action of whatsoever character which the City may incur, sustain or be subjected to on account of loss or damage to property or loss of use thereof, or for bodily injury to or death of any person arising out of or in any way connected to the encroachment; 2) A license agreement shall be submitted to reimburse the City for any costs incurred by the City to repair damage, restore premises, or satisfy claims incurred by reason of the encroachment; and 3) The entire outdoor patio area and deck are denied. The applicant shall submit a Revised Neighborhood Compatibility application and new Grading Permit application for any proposed outdoor patio/deck improvements.
d.
NC-1543/G-1560/M-1064/M-1065-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 709 Via Somonte. Lot 11, Block 1538, Tract 6884. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.
Applicant/
Owner: GA Design Inc.
Action: Approved the application (3-2 in favor, Welch and Evans dissenting) with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) The non-standard encroachments shall not be located within the first 5 feet behind the curb; 2) 6-inch curb gutter shall be installed along the property frontage. A curb and gutter plan shall be prepared by a Registered Civil Engineer; 3) A license agreement shall be submitted to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the city, its officers, agents and employees from and against any and all loss, damage, liability, claims, demands, costs, charges, and expenses, including attorneyâ€™s fees, and causes of action of whatsoever character which the City may incur, sustain or be subjected to on account of loss or damage to property or loss of use thereof, or for bodily injury to or death of any person arising out of or in any way connected to the encroachment; 4) A license agreement shall be submitted to reimburse the City for any costs incurred by the City to repair damage, restore premises, or satisfy claims incurred by reason of the encroachment; 5) The overall ridge height of the residence shall be reduced by 1 ft.; and 6) Landscaping shall not exceed the height of the roof ridgeline.
e.
CUP-90-16; Consideration of a Conditional Use Permit Application to install new tee boxes on holes #15 & 16, to rebuild the greens on holes #15 & 16, and to modify 16 fairway at the Palos Verdes Estates Golf Club located at 3301 Via Campesina. Portion of B, Tract 4400.
Applicant: Palos Verdes Golf Club/Pat Gradoville
Action: Approved the application (5-0 in favor) with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) Construction details of the proposed foot bridge shall be submitted to confirm there will be no impacts to the blue line stream, identified as Tributary B1 on Exhibit 1; 2) A construction management plan that identifies the construction schedule and staging areas shall be submitted and approved by the Director or authorized designee prior to the issuance of permits; and 3) A qualified biologist shall conduct a nesting bird survey(s) prior to removing trees, shrubs, tall herbaceous vegetation, and any structures to prevent any violations of the Migratory Bird Treaty Act.
f.
M-1075-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 3821 Via Palomino. Lot 2, Block 6218, Tract 6887. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.
Applicant/
Owner: Tres & Julie Reid
Action: Approved the application (5-0 in favor) with standard conditions.

10.
Annual Protest Hearings Declaring that Weeds, Brush, Rubbish and Refuse Upon or in Front of Specified Properties in the City are a Seasonal and Recurrent Public Nuisance, and Declaring its Intention for the Abatement Thereof
Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council open the protest hearing in accordance with Resolution R16-06 for unimproved properties, and at the conclusion of the hearing, adjust the list according to the protests heard and adopt a minute resolution directing the County Agricultural Commissioner Office (CACO) to inspect and abate weeds, brush, rubbish, and refuse as necessary on unimproved lots contained in the adjusted list; and open the protest hearing in accordance with Resolution R16-07 for improved properties, and direct the Los Angeles County Fire Department (LACFD) to inspect all improved properties before affirmation of the final list.
